biography: Júlio Campos, born amidst the vibrant chaos of Curitiba, Brazil, wasn't raised in the shadow of racetracks, but in the heart of his father's bustling auto repair shop. Grease replaced formula in his early years, but the smell of gasoline ignited a different kind of passion. At 18, he defied his father's wishes to take over the shop and instead scraped together enough money to enter local karting competitions. His aggressive style quickly caught the attention of Copa Montana, providing his breakout opportunity. Years with Prati-Donaduzzi Racing and a long stint under the Lubrax Podium banner cemented his reputation as a consistent contender, though never quite a champion. Now in his mid-thirties and with Pole Motorsport, Campos faces the harsh reality of a sport that favors youth. The podium finishes are fewer, the challenges greater, but the fire still burns, even if it flickers more than it roars.
drivingStyle: Campos is known for his flamboyant, almost reckless driving style. He's an aggressive late-braker, often pushing his car to the absolute limit through corners, sometimes beyond. Tire management isn't his forte; he prefers to extract maximum pace early in a stint, sacrificing longevity for immediate gains. Under pressure, Campos tends to become even more aggressive, leading to spectacular overtakes or costly mistakes. He's a risk-taker, a gambler on four wheels.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision in the 2018 Stock Car Pro Series, Vargas accused Campos of intentional wrecking, leading to heated exchanges both on and off the track.
A fierce on-track competitor known for her cool and calculated approach, Flores often clashes with Campos's more aggressive tactics, resulting in several wheel-to-wheel battles and near misses.
Mendes, a rising star, openly criticized Campos's 'outdated' driving style, sparking a war of words and intensifying their competition for track position.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, regardless of the weather.
Listens to a specific 80s rock anthem before every race.
Refuses to eat anything green on race days.
famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser.
careerHighlight: Winning the 2017 Curitiba Stock Car race in front of his home crowd, a victory he dedicated to his father, who finally acknowledged his racing career.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2020 Interlagos race due to an overly ambitious overtaking maneuver, costing him a potential championship.
